result.markdown:
For a small customer support team, I'd prioritize **ease of use, affordable per-agent pricing, shared inbox functionality, automation, and room to grow** rather than choosing the most feature-heavy platform.

My recommendation is to start with **Freshdesk or Help Scout**\. Both are strong options for small teams, but they serve slightly different needs.

Here are the platforms I'd put on your shortlist.

## Best help desk software compared

![Freshdesk Logo PNG Vector, Icon Free Download](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/6qU8kcZ34jjxaMCtOBf7YWhzyOSb4fLSOT_GPJYQYIx24a7PwWoi7hpZo4x509_4b3-kIDLNQe_ItQQEi-WAvlGt3qon3gqgkkzkVJ7rlKkd7YLr912Nq6y7Vk1Uu5WARnpY3GOispDCTHWQEF5GWM56LXxTfHKwJYwpAR5GCS7-znnYRHScTTJZc1y6rm-b?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. Freshdesk**

(Best overall)

# \$19

Per agent/month, annual billing (USD)

- Ticket management and automation
- Knowledge base and self-service
- Reporting and AI capabilities
- Good balance of simplicity and functionality

Best for: Small teams that want a traditional help desk that can scale.

[Freshdesk website](https://www.freshworks.com/freshdesk/)

---



**2\. Help Scout**

(Best for simplicity)

# \$25

Per user/month, annual billing (USD); free plan available

- Shared email inbox
- Collision detection to prevent duplicate replies
- Customer conversation history
- Knowledge base and workflows

Best for: Teams handling mostly email support that want a friendly, straightforward experience.

[Help Scout website](https://www.helpscout.com/)

**3\. Zoho Desk**

(Best budget option)

# \$7

Per user/month, annual billing (USD), Express plan

- Ticket management
- Workflow automation
- Customer support reporting
- Integrates with Zoho CRM

Best for: Small teams looking to keep software costs low.

[Zoho Desk website](https://www.zoho.com/desk/)

---

![CXPA Global | CX Day](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/Df7ZME9U6OBHF5y7Iy8re15rfxWfkij2J5upWOY6h17xPwPTHy9GzGMO1pjPycv2eahYGXuZJQqpk7Eu-n45330bnP145JuZvq23mLa9ySgQfmrjrLanGhUx6oyklDReusakKYD0C0EVNYz4WHwYHTEn8t4EiNn2pI71GHk_6Pu88F0xspYAogvoagE-Nhjq?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Zendesk**

# \$19

Per agent/month, annual billing (USD), Support Team plan

- Advanced ticket workflows
- Extensive integrations
- Strong reporting capabilities
- Scalable customer service infrastructure

Best for: Teams expecting significant growth or more complex support operations. More advanced omnichannel functionality costs extra.

[Zendesk website](https://www.zendesk.com/)

---

![Intercom Logo Png | Intercom Logo Vector  - freepng](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/vFOQbMyn2j-qrEP5MHp3qoFYnuQRn1cNIfnWQhDFvgh95R4Cu49za2tFfEkvIv79ilMOFzjbFGwYrtuH93CcstvlD3cBng8uXgV3IJzFRe-TxAtkUNFzghajwFIC5oqM0n811yv9-C9TOqn_W609T7kEkg8E881i6YYXxNOIfT__6enTpEmRSc-AaYfiQh2H?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. Intercom**

# \$29

Per seat/month, annual billing, Essential plan

- Live chat and messaging
- AI customer service agent
- Automated responses
- In-app customer support

Best for: SaaS businesses and teams that handle lots of website or in-app conversations.

[Intercom website](https://www.intercom.com/)

## Quick comparison

| Software | Ease of use | Best strength |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Freshdesk | Easy | Complete ticketing |
| Help Scout | Very easy | Email support |
| Zoho Desk | Moderate | Affordability |
| Zendesk | Moderate | Advanced workflows |
| Intercom | Easy | Live chat and AI |


## What I'd look for before choosing

For a small support team, I'd make sure the software includes\:

1. **Shared inbox\:** Everyone can see and manage customer requests.
2. **Ticket assignment\:** Each issue has a clear owner.
3. **Automation\:** Automatically assign, categorize and prioritize tickets.
4. **Knowledge base\:** Customers can find answers themselves.
5. **Reporting\:** Track response times, resolution times and ticket volume.
6. **Integrations\:** Connect email, CRM, website chat and other business tools.

## Let me narrow it down to the best one

There are a few important differences depending on how your support team operates.
